core_obligations: Choose a K-flat representative of the given complex and replace each derived tensor product by an ordinary total tensor product (proof lines 14821-14860).
Verify that the replacements do not change the objects up to quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 14860-14875).
Identify the two sides by associativity, obtaining the comparison of the statement (proof lines 14875-14891).
proof_roadmap: Replace the derived tensor products and check quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 14860-14875).
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares two ways of forming a double derived base change of a complex, and the proof is a 71-line argument through K-flat resolutions. It chooses a K-flat representative of the complex, replaces each derived tensor product by an ordinary total tensor product against that representative, and identifies the two sides by associativity together with the K-flatness that legitimises the replacement. The choice of resolution and the two replacements are the steps a reader has to follow, and both are displayed.
